- When sentiment is consistently negative (0.00) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive (1.00) and price is falling, model underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–3% to match sentiment-driven mean reversion.
- In low-sentiment periods (all 0.00), model tends to overestimate mean reversion; reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period volatility; add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating 0.00/1.00, model exhibits “sentiment lag” — forecast lags 1–2 days behind sentiment shift; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
